gloss: ice pack; cold pack; coolant pack

definitions.gloss: ice pack; cold pack; coolant pack
definitions.explanation: A gel pack that can be frozen and used to keep things cold. Commonly used for keeping food fresh during transport, cooling injuries, or beating the summer heat.

examples.japanese: {保冷剤|ほれいざい}を{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please put in an ice pack.

examples.japanese: ケーキを{買|か}ったとき、{店員|てんいん}が{保冷剤|ほれいざい}を{付|つ}けてくれた。
examples.english: When I bought the cake, the clerk included an ice pack.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{保冷剤|ほれいざい}をタオルに{包|つつ}んで{首|くび}に{巻|ま}くと{涼|すず}しい。
examples.english: In summer, wrapping an ice pack in a towel and putting it around your neck keeps you cool.

notes:
USAGE: {保冷剤|ほれいざい} is an everyday word in Japan. Cake shops and other stores selling perishable goods routinely offer {保冷剤|ほれいざい} with purchases. They are also commonly used in {保冷|ほれい}バッグ (insulated bags) for picnics and lunch boxes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {保冷剤|ほれいざい}を{入|い}れる (to put in an ice pack)
- {保冷剤|ほれいざい}を{付|つ}ける (to include an ice pack)
- {保冷剤|ほれいざい}を{冷凍庫|れいとうこ}で{凍|こお}らせる (to freeze an ice pack in the freezer)

The word is a compound of {保冷|ほれい} (keeping cold) and {剤|ざい} (agent/substance). In cake shops, you may be asked {保冷剤|ほれいざい}はお{付|つ}けしますか (Shall I include an ice pack?).
